title: What belongs in retrieval, per side of the aisle, and what deliberately does not
prose: The retrieval index covers 777 files, so 'in the RAG or out of it' is the wrong cut -- almost everything is in the index. What differs is what a reader should QUERY to answer a question versus what they should go READ. Five buckets, and three of them are checkable: a knowledge file must exist, an excluded path must genuinely be absent from the index, and a not_written path must genuinely not exist yet. That last one is the useful direction -- when somebody creates a file listed as not_written, ownership_gate reports the table as stale, so filling a known gap tells you to update the record instead of silently leaving it lying.

buckets.knowledge: Synthesised, corrected, provenance-bearing. This is what an agent should QUERY. Ranked, weighted, and the only bucket that should normally answer a question.
buckets.source: The implementation. Indexed so it can be FOUND, not so it can answer. Reading code is not retrieval.
buckets.captured: Verbatim upstream reference. Deliberately demoted in ranking by the meta and primary-source rules, so it wins only when the question is explicitly about the upstream source.
buckets.excluded: Not in the index at all: vendored third-party trees, session artefacts, the derived index. Present on disk, findable by path, never retrieved.
buckets.not_written: Does not exist. Listed so the gap is visible and so the table can notice when it stops being true.

sides.summary: Anything that runs inside Fallout4.exe: the Papyrus VM, Layer A and B, records, addresses.
captured: third_party/CommonLibF4/  (indexed: 350 files of engine layout, incl. BSScript.h and VTABLE_IDs.h)

not_written.why: the one unmet engine invariant; needs a class declaration in method order to derive an index. CommonLibF4 holds candidates, nothing is derived yet
designed in structural_layers.md as a NOT_MET invariant, but no byte layout, no record size, no drain protocol

not_written.gap: a measurement of the zero-alloc hot path
not_written.why: the rule is documented in the tier table and asserted by nobody; it is UNVERIFIED, not met

out_of_side_but_relevant.note: The game itself cannot be in any knowledge base. Fallout4.exe is the authority, and CommonLibF4 is the closest proxy we hold.

sides.summary: PIP-MON's own code and contracts, at either placement: natives, the wire, the backend, the surface, and the tooling.
captured: ai_context/systems/F4SE-Plugins/  (structural reference for an extender; NOT a dependency)
ai_context/systems_core/pyo3/  (reference for a PLANNED bridge; PyO3 is not installed)
third_party/zydis/  (vendored disassembler; INDEXED, not excluded -- see note)
third_party/xedit/  (vendored TES5Edit tree; INDEXED, not excluded -- see note)
sides.third_party_note: All of third_party/ is INDEXED, deliberately. CommonLibF4 is how engine structure is found at all -- the BSScript.h lead exists because that tree is searchable. An earlier draft of this table listed zydis and xedit as excluded; ownership_gate caught it, because 'third_party' was never in the indexer's skip list. Binaries are still filtered by extension, so the 274 MB of xedit executables are not in the corpus -- only its 256 source files, CommonLibF4's 350, and zydis's 641.

not_written.gap: a live capability report for the in-house side
not_written.why: spec_lint can tell a component lies about gate_covered, but nothing can yet measure whether the backend is actually reachable at runtime

not_written.gap: the derivation registry beyond a single live entry
not_written.why: selfalign.py has exactly one DERIVED entry today; the mechanism is proven but thin, and the count should not imply more automation than exists

out_of_side_but_relevant.note: The wire contract deliberately sits OUTSIDE the corrected layer, because it is partly fiction.
paths: docs/IPC_PROTOCOL.md (three of ten payload sizes were wrong on audit; still documents a priority-drop scheme, a control channel and a config file that do not exist)

sides.summary: Anything at authoring time: the CK, its addons, headless xEdit, and the validation tooling.

not_written.why: the load is proven at ~2m15s but no run has ever produced a report; the corrected script is unproven end to end
CKPE is absent, three crash dumps are on record, and Cell View list virtualisation is a candidate rather than a diagnosis
the CK has no scriptable interface on this machine, so every editor-facing tool is read-only by necessity

out_of_side_but_relevant.note: The creation-kit x L-IN cell is empty and cannot be filled: authoring-time and running-game are different worlds.
